title: Tide and Letters
premise: Sebastian Brightwater keeps her late grandfather's lighthouse on the Cornish coast, writing novels by day and refusing, by stubborn discipline, to feel anything she can't control. When a snowstorm traps her with Julian Ashe and Theo Marchetti — the two men who shattered her heart in their twenties over a single unsent letter — old rivalries reignite and the truth of that decade-old mistake finally surfaces. As the storm isolates them for a week, Sebastian must choose between the safe fiction she's written about her own heart and the messy, living truth: that love isn't trainable, it's inherited, like the lighthouse itself. She ends the silence with the sentence she rehearsed for ten years, choosing neither man outright but herself first — and finding that one of them waited long enough to be chosen second.
about_author: Mirabel Whitlock is a former archivist who spent five years cataloguing unsent letters in coastal estate collections before turning to fiction full-time. She lives in a converted signal station with an opinionated cat named Beacon.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Establishes her ordered life at the lighthouse: morning rituals, her half-finished novel, and the locked tin box containing one letter she's never sent. Her editor calls demanding the book's ending; Sebastian insists hearts are muscles you can train. Emotional beat: controlled solitude masking grief for her grandfather.

chapters.title: Two Cars in the Snow
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A freak snowstorm strands two travelers on the coast road — Julian Ashe and Theo Marchetti, rivals since university, both forced to shelter at the lighthouse. The recognition scene is electric and awful: these are the two men from the worst night of her twenties. Emotional beat: shock curdling into defensive anger.

chapters.title: Rationed Candles
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Power fails; the three ration candles and stories by firelight. Julian, now an architect, watches Theo charm Sebastian and remembers why he lost her once already. He finds her manuscript pages and recognizes himself in a villain. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Theo Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals he never stopped writing to Sebastian — letters returned unopened for a decade, kept in his glovebox. We learn the original triangle: both men loved her; she fled before choosing. His tenderness contrasts Julian's strategy. Emotional beat: longing braided with self-reproach.

chapters.title: The Tin Box
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Julian discovers the tin box; inside, not one letter but dozens — drafts of the same sentence, rehearsed for ten years, addressed to no one. Confrontation: why did she leave? Sebastian deflects into her grandfather's story, revealing the inheritance theme: he too chose the lighthouse over a person. Emotional beat: exposure without confession.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm worsens; roads close entirely. Trapped together, old rivalry turns physical — a fight in the snow over who 'deserves' a second chance. Sebastian stops it cold: she is not a prize. First real honesty between all three. Emotional beat: fury breaking open into vulnerability.

chapters.title: Letters Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. By candlelight, Theo reads his returned letters aloud; Julian counters by reading Sebastian's own draft sentences back to her. The decade-old mistake is fully revealed: each man believed the other was chosen, so both withdrew. Emotional beat: devastating mutual misunderstanding laid bare.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax. Storm breaks at dawn; rescue nears, meaning time runs out. Sebastian speaks the rehearsed sentence at last — but it isn't a choice between the men. It's a vow to stop containing her own heart, spoken to herself, witnessed by them. Both men must decide what they want without her permission. Emotional beat: liberation through terrifying honesty.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Roads clear; Theo leaves first, gracefully, asking only for one opened letter. Julian stays to help repair storm damage, no longer competing, just present. Sebastian finishes her novel's ending — changing the villain into a man who waits. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning, hope without guarantee.

chapters.title: Return Address
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Spring. A letter arrives — Theo's, finally opened — and beneath it, Julian's answer to her sentence: patience, offered freely. Sebastian lights the lighthouse lamp for the season, understanding inheritance as something chosen, not owed. Final image: she mails a letter of her own, addressed at last. Emotional beat: earned, open-ended peace.
